note: Documented cases found by web search on 21 October 2026. Each claim is what the cited source reports. Where sources disagree, the case says so. A record may cite a case from this pool only; any other claim must be written as an inference from the model's principle.

cases.claim: In 1979 a master's degree became the minimum qualification for teaching in general education. Class teachers, who had trained on a three-year bachelor-level programme, moved to a five-year master's in educational sciences. Elementary and secondary teachers share one master's-level bar and equal academic rank. Accounts differ on when teacher training moved into the universities (1971 or 1974).
cases.source: Paper on teacher education in Finland in the Croatian journal Hrcak; Niemi, journal article on Finnish teacher education (2013)
cases.caveat: These sources cover training and academic rank, not pay or legal status. The dates and programme lengths differ between accounts.

cases.case: Teacher pay and status in the Soviet 1930s
cases.claim: Pay levels for rural teachers in the 1930s are not confirmed by these results. Ewing's 2002 study places village instructors between state policy and a population that resisted it. A Dagestan study by Kaimarazov and Kaimarazova draws on unpublished archives on teachers' housing, pay and pensions in the 1930s, but its abstract gives no baseline pay figures.
cases.source: Ewing, Teachers of Stalinism (2002), as reviewed in Australian Slavonic and East European Studies (2004); Kaimarazov and Kaimarazova, Dagestan teachers in the 1930s
cases.caveat: No verified pay figure for the Soviet 1930s. Read Ewing and the Dagestan study before writing any pay claim for the Soviet Union.

cases.case: China's Teachers Law and the parity of teachers' pay
cases.claim: The Teachers Law was passed in late October 1993 and took effect in January 1994; it was revised in 2009. It places teachers on a par with local civil servants, and its pay and welfare provisions sit in the chapter on material benefits. Rules on pay were never fully enforced: in 2008 and 2009 rural teachers in Chongqing were paid roughly a third, and sometimes a quarter, of what other government staff earned, and rural teachers struck for their pay.
cases.source: China Labour Bulletin, rural teachers' strikes for promised higher pay (April 2009); CECC English text of the Teachers Law of the People's Republic of China
cases.caveat: The enforcement figures describe 2008 and 2009, not later years. The article number of the parity clause is not confirmed; read the CECC text before citing it.

cases.case: Teacher pay compared with graduates across the OECD
cases.claim: In the 2026 Education at a Glance, teachers' pay in primary and general secondary education runs at about 87 to 95 per cent of the pay of tertiary graduates, on average across the OECD. School leaders earn more than half again as much as teachers at these levels. The ratio fell by one percentage point between 2015 and 2023, though the variation between countries is large.
cases.source: OECD, Education at a Glance 2026, indicator on how much teachers and school heads are paid
cases.caveat: The averages are OECD-wide. Country figures are in the full tables, which the results did not show.
